instagram_prompts: First-person perspective (FPP) optic sensor capture from nanobot scale, fixed-mount 14mm ultrawide lens, deep depth of field. Hovering centimeters above the rain-wet Rheingasse cobblestones in Basel's Kleinbasel quarter, Switzerland. Ancient rounded cobblestones fill the foreground — worn so smooth they're almost polished, catching orange streetlamp reflections in wet pools. Mid-ground: the ornate 1873 facade of Hotel Krafft, warm amber light spilling from arched windows onto the slick stone. Beyond it, the pewter Rhine, and across the water, the red sandstone Basler Münster cathedral tower against an overcast dusk sky. Deep in the background, the Roche Tower — a glass monolith lit pharmaceutical-white — rises above the medieval roofline. Scale is enormous. The cobblestones loom like boulders. Palette: Basel heraldic red, pharmaceutical white, pewter river, amber lamp. Cold late-afternoon. No text or overlays (background use only).

First-person perspective (FPP) optic sensor capture from nanobot scale, fixed-mount 14mm ultrawide lens, deep depth of field. Hovering millimeters above a polished laboratory benchtop inside a Basel biotech facility. In the immediate foreground: a single clear glass vial containing a pale green liquid — enormous from this perspective, like a glass tower. Behind it, a row of identical vials receding into sharp depth-of-field blur. Mid-ground: stainless steel equipment — pipette arm, centrifuge rotor — all gleaming under cool fluorescent light. Through the lab window in the background: the pewter Rhine river and the red-stone spire of the Basler Münster, framing the ancient city beyond the glass. The contrast is the composition — precision instruments and medieval stone, present tense and 15th century, both sharp. Palette: pharmaceutical white, frosted glass green, stainless steel, Basel-red sandstone in background. Fluorescent-cool interior. No text or overlays (background use only).

First-person perspective (FPP) optic sensor capture from nanobot scale, fixed-mount 14mm ultrawide lens, deep depth of field. Hovering inside a bioreactor flask, looking out through curved borosilicate glass. The glass curves the entire world beyond it into a fish-eye distortion: a Basel laboratory bench visible through the transparent culture medium, which is a pale amber-gold broth — the engineered microbes invisible to the naked eye but thick in the medium surrounding the sensor. Beyond the glass: a researcher's white-coated arm, blurred. Further back: a window overlooking the Rhine and the Novartis campus towers across the water. The scale is extraordinary — the meniscus of the liquid curves overhead like a sky. Everything outside the flask is distorted by the curvature of the glass and the refraction of the culture medium. Palette: amber broth, pharmaceutical white, cobalt Novartis blue in distance, frosted glass, Rhine pewter. No text or overlays (background use only).
